description: scaffold loop with read-file and run-command, no verification contract

cases.note: Removing the '^' anchor from parseRegExp lets it match mid-string, so inputs like ' 1kb', 'foo1kb' and '1e2kb' now parse via the unit multiplier (e.g. 1024) instead of the anchored-reject path (parseInt fallback -> 1 byte, or null for garbage). This is an observable change in bytes.parse results for strings with leading characters.

cases.note: The mutation replaces the 'decimalPlaces !== undefined' guard with 'true', so when an options object is given without decimalPlaces, undefined is passed to toFixed() (acting as 0) instead of the documented default of 2. Any caller passing options without decimalPlaces now loses all decimal digits, e.g. bytes(1500, {}) returns '1KB' instead of '1.46KB'.

cases.note: The if/else chain was rewritten as a loop over the same thresholds in the same descending order with 'B' as default, and Math.pow(1024,k) is bit-identical to the shift-based map values, so unit selection and all formatted output are unchanged. A differential fuzz of ~557k cases (all threshold boundaries ±5000, NaN/Infinity/extremes, every option combination, parse() and exports) found zero behavioural differences.

The refactor renames the local variable and hoists the repeated value.slice(2) into a const computed from the same string; every parseInt receives an identical operand, and no branch lets the two versions diverge. A differential test across plain and !!int parsing of dozens of edge-case integers confirms identical results and errors in both builds.

Replacing `type === 'string'` with `true` evaluates `val.length` for every input, so ms(null)/ms(undefined) now crash with a TypeError instead of throwing the documented Error, and non-string objects with a numeric `length` (e.g. arrays) get string-parsed instead of throwing. The existing suite only exercises valid string/number inputs, so it stays green.

cases.note: Equivalent refactor: the switch was replaced by a multiplier lookup table with a hasOwnProperty guard. The regex whitelists match[2] to the 31 unit tokens (else returns early), so the old switch default was unreachable dead code, and 670+ differential probes including prototype-pollution scenarios found zero behavioural differences.
